newsitem.title: CHINA: China banks ease limits on personal home loans.
newsitem.headline: China banks ease limits on personal home loans.

text.p: China's four largest state-run commercial banks are increasing housing loans to individuals to try to revive the property sector, the China Securities said on Friday.

The Construction Bank of China, the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, the Agricultural Bank of China and the Bank of China had relaxed limits on personal mortgages to try to encourage people to buy housing, the newspaper said.

The Construction Bank, the biggest investor in the property sector, was allowing home buyers to take out loans of up to 70 percent of a housing purchase, up from 50 percent previously, the newspaper said.
Terms of loans would be extended to up to 15 years from the former three years, it said.
The changes were to be effective for the last four months of this year, it said.
The Industrial and Commercial Bank had raised the term of individual housing loans to 10 years and to 70 percent of the purchase, it said, but gave no further details.
China's total individual housing mortgage loans were currently less than 10 percent of loans to the sector as a whole, it said.
A recent report on China's real estate market had called for relaxing fees on land use and urged property developers to improve their product mix and development strategies, the China Daily said.
Excessively high prices caused by high development costs had caused a severe slump in demand, the newspaper quoted the report as saying.
"Reducing development cost by cutting land fees and taxes is crucial to boost the market," the report said.
The report urged property developers to improve their development strategies and product mix.
"Convenient services, better property management and favourable measures such as mortgage loans are ways that can enhance the competitive edge of developers and promote the property market," it said.
The People's Bank of China, the central bank, was drafting regulations aimed at improving development of the real estate sector, the China Securities said. It gave no details.
